Subject: Re: ProspectCo redlines — output ownership & commercial carveouts

Samantha — thanks for the note and the redline. Looping in Ben (account lead) and Laura (legal) to triage. Quick summary of Redwood’s high-level position so everyone is aligned before Laura proposes language: 

- Core principle: Customers retain ownership of Customer Data and Outputs generated from their data and prompts; we typically confirm that in the MSA/order form.
- Feedback/learning: Redwood asks for a limited, non-exclusive license to use anonymized or aggregated feedback and telemetry to improve the service; this is not intended to give us rights to reassign or resell Customer-specific Outputs.
- Commercialization ask: Redwood does not typically assert ownership of end-customer outputs. We also do not generally seek revenue share on customer-owned outputs. If ProspectCo is proposing a clause where Redwood would commercialize derivatives of ProspectCo Outputs, that’s a non-standard path and would need explicit, negotiated commercial terms (and signoff).

Laura — can you propose redline language that: (a) reaffirms Customer Output ownership; (b) provides Redwood a narrow feedback license for product improvement only; (c) defines the pathway (if any) for separate commercialization deals so there’s a clear escalation path instead of a default grant?

Samantha — we should be able to come back with suggested language within 24h. If your team is open, Ben and I can host a short call tomorrow to align commercial expectations.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: ProspectCo redlines — proposed legal language

Folks — draft language below that I recommend we propose to ProspectCo. I’m attaching our tracked changes version for their counsel (legal_markups_track_changes.docx). The text is deliberately conservative on rights; if Sales wants a looser commercial stance we can adjust.

--- PROPOSED ORDER FORM LANGUAGE (for inclusion in Order Form / MSA) ---

1) Customer Output Ownership. 
Customer retains all right, title, and interest in and to Customer Data and Output ("Customer Outputs"). For clarity, "Output" means the content generated by Redwood in response to Customer prompts or inputs. Except as expressly set forth in this Agreement, Redwood does not acquire any rights to Customer Outputs.

2) Feedback and Product Improvement License. 
Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, perpetual license to use Feedback (defined as feedback, anonymized usage data, aggregate telemetry, and de-identified prompts) to develop, improve, and operate Redwood’s services, provided that such Feedback is not reasonably capable of being re-associated with Customer or Customer Outputs. Feedback does not include Customer Outputs.

3) Commercialization of Customer-Specific Outputs. 
Neither party will commercialize Customer Outputs belonging to the other party without the other party’s prior written consent. If the parties mutually agree that Redwood may commercialize certain derivative products that incorporate Customer Outputs, the parties shall negotiate in good faith a separate written commercial agreement setting forth the scope, compensation (if any), confidentiality, and data governance terms.

4) Optional: Revenue Share (only if separately agreed). 
Any revenue-sharing arrangement referenced in section 3 must be set forth in a separate executed agreement. Neither party shall be deemed to have agreed to revenue sharing, assignment, or transfer of Customer Outputs by virtue of the license granted in section 2.

--- end proposed language ---

Notes: 
- The suggested approach is: keep the Order Form clean on ownership, allow Redwood product improvement use via a narrow Feedback license, and require a separate commercial agreement if either party wants Redwood to commercialize derivatives that include Customer Outputs.
- I recommend we proactively propose the separate commercial path rather than a revenue-share default; revenue share is a commercial negotiation and should live in a commercial addendum.

I attached legal_markups_track_changes.docx containing tracked edits against their redline.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 10:10:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: ProspectCo redlines — commercial perspective

Quick commercial take — Rafael / Laura, I agree with the legal framing but want to flag commercial sensitivities: 

- ProspectCo’s execs asked about revenue share likely because they want protection if Redwood productizes their outputs. We should avoid committing to any revenue share in the Order Form.
- Proposed customer-facing compromise: offer a limited pathway: Redwood can propose a joint commercialization pilot (separate SOW) where if Redwood builds a product that uses ProspectCo Outputs materially, then ProspectCo gets first right to co-develop or an agreed commercial uplift (credit, referral fee, or negotiated share). That keeps the Order Form simple and gives them the runway they want.
- Market ask: include a carveout for marketing/marketplace references (Redwood can reference ProspectCo in case studies with opt-out) — this is often important for our GTM.

If the customer presses on revenue share in the Order Form, we should push back and use the separate-deal path. Happy to join the call and frame it as a standard enterprise pattern.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
